inputs.text:
Look at what is happening to our society when the state decides to replace personal responsibility with handouts. Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has rolled out a manifesto that literally doubles women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 and hands out Rs 8,000 household coupons. Instead of encouraging traditional family values, personal responsibility, and the dignity of earned work, this administration is actively expanding the welfare state to foster a culture of dependency.

They wrap it in nice-sounding talk about targeting labor and redistributive measures for vulnerable groups, but we all know what the actual result is: it undermines self-reliance and weakens the foundational role of the traditional household. On top of this aggressive wealth redistribution, they are throwing around free motor pumpsets to farmers and enhancing support for fishermen, while just paying lip service to capitalist FDI growth and technocratic AI development. 

When the government inserts itself this deeply into the economy to pick winners and losers, it completely erodes traditional authority. True community strength comes from hard work and traditional values, not from government checks and socialist engineering.
